title: Account-aware intake funnel and rapid-scope rubric for enterprise asks
creator: Evan Brooks
description:
Problem: Sales and CS regularly forward enterprise feature asks that are high-value but heterogeneous in scope, making it hard for PM and Eng to triage quickly. Existing playbooks are focused on bulk aggregation rather than account-aware urgency, which leads to missed contract opportunities and long lead times.

Goal: Define a lightweight, account-aware intake funnel and rapid-scope rubric that (1) segments requests by account tier and contractual triggers, (2) produces a 1-page micro-PRD and effort band within 48 hours for high-value asks, and (3) runs a two-week pilot with two AMs to validate decisioning and handoff.

What this ticket delivers: a) taxonomy for account tiers and triggers (SLA clauses, upcoming renewals, proof-of-value opportunities), b) prioritization scorecard combining business impact, technical risk, and operational cost, c) a 1-page micro-PRD template (problem, hypothesis, success metrics, roll-forward plan), d) effort-banding matrix (QuickFix 1-2d, ShortProject 1-3w, EngProject 1-3m) with cost ranges, e) a minimal automation spreadsheet and triage playbook for Sales/CS to use when submitting requests.

Out of scope: building a full-featured intake app, changes to pricing/contract language, engineering implementation of feature work beyond initial scoping artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Taxonomy document that maps account tiers (Pilot/Startup, Growth, Strategic, Enterprise) to urgency triggers and expected internal SLA for triage is published
Micro-PRD template exists and can be populated in < 48 hours for a flagged enterprise ask
Prioritization scorecard defined with weighting and example scoring for five historical asks
Effort-banding matrix with three buckets and representative engineering-day cost ranges published
Pilot completed with two AMs and at least 6 incoming asks through the funnel; pilot retrospective and list of adjustments delivered
notes: Emphasize minimal friction for Sales/CS: the submission flow must be usable in a single call or via a one-page form. Design should avoid heavy fields; scorecard calculations should be automated in the spreadsheet so AMs get immediate suggested prioritization. Coordinate with Solutions Engineering for technical viability checks. Consider quick legal/contract flags (renewal within 90 days, committed spend increase) as priority bumps.
